question.leadin: The term "Deluge" refers to a period in which Sweden occupied a union of these two countries, which was governed by a parliament called the sejm (same).
question.text: Name these two countries that signed the 1569 Union of Lublin, unifying into a commonwealth that would last until it lost its land in a series of 18th century partitions.
question.answerHtml: Poland and Lithuania [or the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, or Korona Królestwa Polskiego and Didi Kunigystė Lietuvos or the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]
question.clue: The head of one of these countries instigated Zeligowski's Mutiny in the other.

swap.text: This man won the first free Polish election in 1990 after using his leverage as leader of Solidarity to push back Soviet influence at the Roundtable talks.
swap.clue: His wife, Danuta, claimed his Nobel Peace Prize for him in 1983.

question.leadin: A radio mast in this city was the tallest manmade structure in the world prior to its collapse in 1991.
question.text: Name this capital city on the Vistula River. The most famous anti-Nazi Jewish uprising occurred in this city's ghetto, where the Muranow neighborhood was built after the war using "rubble-concrete" from the destroyed buildings.
question.clue: A forest near this city was the site of a facility built under Operation Reinhard in the village of Treblinka (treb-LINK-ah).

swap.leadin: The firing of Anna Walentynowicz triggered a strike that led to the creation of this group.
swap.text: Name this trade union that grew from the 21 MKS Demands developed at the Gdansk shipyards.
swap.clue: The first prime minister elected from this organization spoke of the "thick line" that would demarcate his policies compared to the past.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the November Uprising.
question.text: This city in modern-day Poland was annexed by Austria in the wake of the November Uprising, losing its "Free City" status that had been granted by the Congress of Vienna. This city was the capital of Poland before Warsaw.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.leadin: Answer the following about figures in the Scientific Revolution.
swap.text: The Scientific Revolution is often said to have begun with the publication of On the Revolutions of Heavenly Spheres by this astronomer and proponent of heliocentrism.
swap.clue: In his most famous work, which he dedicated to Pope Paul III, he preserved the concept of "epicycles" and attempted to explain patterns of retrograde motion.

question.text: This once-hotly contested, resource-rich region was annexed by Frederick the Great in 1740, beginning the War of the Austrian Succession.
question.answerHtml: Silesia [accept Slask or Slezsko or Schlesien or Schläsing or Slunsk or Slazynska or Sleska]
question.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Warsaw Pact nations in 1989.
swap.text: Lech Walesa became the first President of this country after leading the Solidarity trade union. This country's capital is Warsaw.
swap.clue: Another man from this modern-day country fortified West Point, making Benedict Arnold's life difficult.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about pre-modern anti-Semitism.
question.text: In eastern Europe, Jews were confined largely to these autonomous villages within the Pale of Settlement, which were often beset by pogroms.
question.clue: Eastern European Jews commonly lived in these small, Yiddish-speaking villages found in Poland-Lithuania and, later, the Pale of Settlement.

swap.text: Jogaila was the Grand Duke of what became this Baltic nation with a capital at Vilnius.
swap.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

question.leadin: This polity incorporated the Duchy of Livonia into its realm during the Livonian War.
question.text: Name this polity that officially formed following the Union of Lublin. This polity's Golden Liberty gave the liberum veto to all members of the Sejm ("same").
question.answerHtml: Poland–Lithuania [accept either underlined portion; accept Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; accept Grand Duchy of Lithuania]
question.clue: A post-Jagiellonian king of this nation allied with Leopold I to break the 1683 siege of Vienna.

swap.text: This man was made First Secretary of Poland's Communist Party in 1981 with instructions to crush Solidarity, which he nearly did, though his befuddlement at Poland's economic stagnation throughout the 1980s opened the door to liberalization.
swap.clue: In 2008, the IPN put this man on trial brutal crackdown which entrenched him as dictator in 1982.

question.leadin: A "general crisis" named for this century led to a population decline in Europe and possibly other parts of the world.
question.text: Name this century, in which both the Thirty Years' War and the Dutch Golden Age ended.
question.clue: 27 Czech leaders were executed in Prague's Old Town Square during this century, partially as revenge for an earlier event in which Ferdinand II's Catholic representatives were hurled out a window.

swap.text: About a century and a half later, the Ottomans once again tried to take Vienna, but were repulsed by one of the largest military charges in history. These cavalry troops under John III Sobieski led the charge.
swap.clue: A commander of these people declared, "We came, we saw, God conquered," during one battle.

question.leadin: Gallus Anonymus wrote a history of this dynasty, whose mythical founder was a wheelwright who succeeded the evil King Popiel after he was eaten alive by mice.
question.text: Mieszko I ("m'YESH-ko the first") was the first historical ruler of what Polish dynasty?
question.clue: The semi-legendary namesake of this dynasty was a wheelwright who was legendarily visited by two angels in disguise who blessed his cellar.

swap.leadin: Name these periods from medieval Eastern Europe.
swap.text: This 1648 to 1667 period in Poland saw large territorial losses to Russia and Sweden; it ended with the abdication of Jan II and the signing of the Truce of Andrusovo.
swap.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

question.text: Before Walesa was elected, this Polish general briefly served as President of Poland after the office's restoration. As Prime Minister, this man initiated the Round Table Talks that resulted in free Polish elections.
question.clue: Before his presidency, he was struck with a case of photokeratitis, which is why he continuously wears sunglasses in public.

swap.text: The election of Henry of Valois followed the 1572 death of this Polish king, the last of the Jagellon dynasty. He himself was succeded by Stephen Bathory, who brought the Livonian War to a conclusion.
swap.clue: This man was the last Jagiellonian king to rule Poland. He oversaw the height of the Polish Reformation and expanded his kingdom into Livonia and Russia.

question.leadin: Name the following about leaders of Lithuania.
question.text: This Lithuanian prince became King of Poland under the Union of Krewo [krevo] and founded a namesake dynasty that variously ruled Lithuania, Poland, Hungary, and Bohemia.
question.clue: This man concluded the Peace of Thorn after defeating Grandmaster Ulrich von Jungingen (OOL-rick von YOUNG-ing-in) of the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Grunwald.

swap.leadin: Eric Hobsbawm characterized the start of this period as a "major servile upheaval" during the 17th-century "General Crisis."
swap.text: Give this term for the chaotic period after the Khmelnytsky Uprising in Ukraine, when the Hetmanate's Left and Right Banks were divided. It overlapped with the Polish-Lithuanian Deluge.
